# Citations

All sources were fetched in-session on **2026-08-21** via the host-side fetch
service. Tier definitions follow the `cited-research` convention:

- **Tier 1** — official vendor documentation, official product repository,
  specification site
- **Tier 2** — established reference site, major engineering org
- **Tier 3** — industry blog, practitioner site
- **Tier 4** — forum, GitHub issue thread, crowd-sourced

A recurring caveat applies to every `developers.openai.com` and
`learn.chatgpt.com` page in this list: **none of them states a publication or
last-updated date.** The dated sources in this pool are: the Codex changelog
[6], the OpenAI research post [31] (2026-02-23), the Anthropic announcement
[61] (2026-05-06), the OpenAI security blog [87] (2026-05-08), the practitioner
posts [89] (2026-08-03), [90] (2026-06-22) and [91] (2026-07-15), the two
help-centre articles carrying relative dates [33][34], and every GitHub issue,
pull request and discussion. Everything else is undated and is cited as "as
fetched 2026-08-21".

A second recurring caveat: `learn.chatgpt.com/docs/*` serves several pages that
are **byte-identical** to their `developers.openai.com/codex/*` counterparts.
Where that is the case it is noted. Two citations to the same sentence on two
hostnames is one source, not corroboration.

Added 2026-08-21 in the same session, when observability was approved as a

deliverable's Limitations section.

## Anthropic — Claude Code telemetry

**[71]** Anthropic. *Monitoring usage*. <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage>
— Tier 1. **The authoritative Claude Code telemetry reference**, and the single
richest source in this dimension. Supplied: `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY`;
the exporter selectors `OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER` (`console|otlp|prometheus|none`),
`OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER`; protocols `grpc`, `http/json`,
`http/protobuf` with "Claude Code has no default protocol, so set this or the
signal-specific protocol variable for each `otlp` exporter you enable"; the
full transport, interval and mTLS variable list; the five cardinality toggles
(`OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID` default `true`, `_VERSION` default `false`,
`_ACCOUNT_UUID` default `true`, `_ENTRYPOINT` default `false`,
`_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` default `true`); the privacy toggles
`OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, `OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES`,
`OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT`, `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES`;
the meter name `com.anthropic.claude_code`; the **eight metrics** and the
**event catalogue**; the standard attribute set; the span hierarchy; and the
managed-settings enforcement behaviour with its stated limit that exporter
selectors "follow normal per-key precedence" (v2.1.223+). Also: "Cost metrics
are approximations. For official billing data, refer to your API provider."
**Quality note:** no publication date; dates itself only through version gates
such as "Requires Claude Code v2.1.232 or later".

**[72]** Anthropic. *Agent SDK — observability*. <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/observability>
— Tier 1. "Telemetry is off until you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and
choose at least one exporter. The most common configuration sends all three
signals over OTLP HTTP to a collector."; "Tracing is in beta. Span names and
attributes may change between releases."; the `session.id` span attribute and
its suppression via `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID`; `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_DIAG_STDERR`.

**[73]** Anthropic. *Agent SDK — cost tracking*. <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/cost-tracking>
— Tier 1. The mechanism behind the cost figures and its honest limits: "The SDK
computes them locally from a price table bundled at build time, so they can
drift from what you are actually billed when: pricing changes / the installed
SDK version does not recognize a model / billing rules apply that the client
cannot model… **Do not bill end users or trigger financial decisions from these
fields.**" Also the pre-v2.1.214 multi-frame usage bug that "inflated
`claude_code.cost.usage` and `claude_code.token.usage` by roughly one extra
full request per extra frame."

**[88]** *Split `OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID` between logs and metrics*,
anthropics/claude-code issue #70210, opened **2026-06-23**, state **Closed as
not planned**, labelled `stale`. <https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/70210>
— Tier 4. "This is immensely helpful in events/logs, but causes high

— Tier 3 practitioner blog, self-described unofficial. Cited **for a claim this
research checked and partly rejected**: it asserts "Two official pages, two
different stories on what happens when you don't set it." Direct reading of
[1] and [3] shows one page states the runtime default in prose and the other
says "When unset, the client default applies" — silence plus a stated default,
not a contradiction. Its operational advice ("treat unset as on") is correct
and is independently confirmed by [76]; its framing as a documented conflict is
not supported.

`server.port`, `error.type`). Retains the disclaimer "These are initial
Generative AI client metric instruments and attributes but more may be added in
the future."

**[80]** OpenTelemetry. *GenAI attribute registry*. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/main/docs/registry/attributes/gen-ai.md>
— Tier 1. The per-attribute stability enumeration. **118 `Development` badges
and zero `Stable` badges**; the three occurrences of the word "stable" in the
file are prose ("the unique and stable identifier of the GenAI hosted agent
resource"), not stability markers. Also the deprecation records: `gen_ai.system`
→ "use `gen_ai.provider.name` instead", `gen_ai.prompt` → "Removed, no
replacement at this time".

**[81]** OpenTelemetry. *semantic-conventions-genai CHANGELOG*. <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/main/CHANGELOG.md>
— Tier 1. As fetched, contains **only `## Unreleased`** with a Towncrier
placeholder and no released version.

**[82]** OpenTelemetry. *semantic-conventions-genai releases*. <https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/releases>
— Tier 1. **"There aren't any releases here."**

**[83]** OpenTelemetry. *Moved: Generative AI semantic conventions*. <https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/>
— Tier 1, specification site, banner "Semantic conventions 1.44.0". "GenAI

**[84]** OpenTelemetry. *GenAI Attributes (Moved)*. <https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/registry/attributes/gen-ai/>
— Tier 1. "Generative AI (GenAI) attributes have moved to the OpenTelemetry

reads "Moved…", so it carries no literal stability level — the `Development`

**[85]** OpenTelemetry. *Blog index*. <https://opentelemetry.io/blog/>
— Tier 1. Used for a **negative finding**: the 2026 list contains "GenAI

**[89]** Praesidia. *OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions status*,
dated **2026-08-03**. <https://praesidia.ai/blog/opentelemetry-genai-semantic-conventions-status>
— Tier 3 practitioner blog. "every `gen_ai.*` attribute, span, metric, and
event in the OpenTelemetry semantic-conventions registry is marked stability
'Development,' not 'Stable'" and "The new dedicated repository had no tagged
release as of mid-July 2026." **Both claims are corroborated by the primary
sources [79][80][81][82].** Its further attribution of the repository move to

**[90]** Shah, Vatsal. *OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions — agents 2026*,
"Released June 22, 2026". <https://shahvatsal.com/news/opentelemetry-genai-semantic-conventions-agents-2026>
— Tier 3 practitioner blog. **Cited as a refuted claim, retained so the
refutation is auditable.** Asserts the GenAI SIG "has stabilized the GenAI
Semantic Conventions in June 2026… has released the stable specification". This
is contradicted by [79], [80], [81] and [82]. Its supporting detail is also
wrong against the registry [80]: it names `gen_ai.system` (deprecated),
`gen_ai.prompt` (removed), `usage.input_tokens`/`usage.output_tokens` (the real
names are `gen_ai.usage.*`), `gen_ai.response.finish_reason` (the real name is
plural), and `gen_ai.tool.status` (not present).
